title: Hilse og presentere seg — greetings and introductions
goal: Complete a first-meeting exchange by greeting, stating one identity fact, asking the same of the other person, and closing.

objectives.statement: Complete a first-meeting exchange by greeting, stating one identity fact, asking the same of the other person, and closing.

spans.value: It is Monday morning at a small language school in Bergen. Two new students arrive early and wait outside their classroom.
Hei! Jeg heter Mina. Hva heter du?

blocks.translation: Hi! My name is Mina. What’s your name?
Hi, Mina. My name is Jonas.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas complete a simple first-meeting exchange. Each part has a clear job: they greet each other, give one identity fact—their name—ask for the same information, and close the conversation.
A first meeting can be short and still feel complete:
You do not need a long introduction. At this stage, the important skill is keeping the exchange moving from opening to closing.
First checkpoint: Notice what jeg heter means
Read one line from the conversation: Mina says «Jeg heter Mina.» Check what this line means in the exchange.
The most useful general greeting is:
It works in many everyday situations. You can use it when meeting someone for the first time, entering a small shop, or greeting someone you already know.
Norwegian often uses a person’s name directly after the greeting:
The greeting can stand alone, but in a first meeting it naturally leads into your identity fact:

spans.value: The exchange is complete because both speakers know the other person’s name and the conversation has a clear closing.
The same pattern works in a different first-meeting situation. Two people arrive for their first shift at a café.
Hei! Jeg heter Selma. Hva heter du?

blocks.translation: Hi! My name is Selma. What’s your name?

spans.value: Jeg heter Noah. Hyggelig å møte deg.

blocks.translation: My name is Noah. Nice to meet you.

spans.value: Their manager calls them into the kitchen.
The setting changes, but the communicative work stays the same: greeting, name, matching question, and closing.

sections.title: Common problems in the complete exchange

spans.value: Giving a name but not inviting a response
This is understandable, but it may leave the other person unsure whether to continue.

no.value: Hei! Jeg heter Pia. Hva heter du?

en.value: Hi! My name is Pia. What’s your name?

spans.value: This clearly invites the other person into the exchange.
Speaker B has not answered. A natural response gives the requested identity fact:
Jeg heter Mats. Hva heter du?

blocks.translation: My name is Mats. What’s your name?

spans.value: The goodbye is grammatical, but the exchange feels abrupt. A friendly acknowledgment creates a smoother close:
Hyggelig å møte deg. Ha det!
Return to Mina and Jonas outside the classroom. Retell their meeting in your own words while keeping the same four communicative jobs. Use different names, but do not add extra identity information.
Your exchange should include a greeting, one speaker’s name, a question for the other person’s name, the answer, and a friendly closing.
Later that day, Mina and Jonas meet again near the school entrance.

They no longer need to ask each other’s names. Their first exchange worked: each greeted the other, shared a name, asked for the same information, and closed clearly. Now they can recognize and greet each other by name.

Without looking back, produce a complete first-meeting exchange between two named speakers. Include a greeting, one identity fact from each person in response to the matching question, and a natural closing.

prompt.value: Ada and Leo are new neighbours. They meet while waiting for a delayed lift and have only a moment to talk. Write a conversation: greet each other, ask names, introduce yourselves, say something nice, and finish before the lift arrives.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the exchange includes a greeting, a natural two-way introduction of Ada and Leo, a friendly line, and a closing. One name question with the other person’s answer is enough; do not require both people to repeat the same question.

criteria.instruction: The exchange contains a Norwegian greeting.
One person asks the other's name and receives an answer, and both Ada and Leo's names are introduced naturally without repeating a name question after the names are known.
The exchange contains a natural friendly meeting expression.
The exchange ends with a natural closing.
